# ADR-0012: Graph Propagation Scheme

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-29

## Last Verified
2026-10-29 (against `design/gdd/life-support-graph.md` LS-8 to LS-13, LS-15 to LS-18, LS-24 to LS-26, D.1, D.6, D.8 to D.12, D.15, D.16 and Section E "Hooks, order, FAULTED, budget"; ADR-0001, ADR-0003 to ADR-0007 and ADR-0010 (all Proposed); ADR-0011 and ADR-0013 (drafts, unreviewed); the architecture hook schedule; Godot 4.7.2 probes of 2026-10-29 on the editor binary, recorded in Engine Compatibility)

## Decision Makers
Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.

## Summary
The Life-Support Graph must advance five coupled loops (power, fuel, oxygen, coolant, gas and heat exchange) and the failure lifecycle deterministically, inside a spike share of the kernel's P3 budget, and must survive a snapshot taken on any tick. This ADR fixes the propagation scheme: one logical step of twelve fixed phases split across three chained step hooks at divisor `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` (offsets 0, 2, 4), exactly one pass per loop per step with three declared write disciplines (delta accumulators, ordered allocation, own-row), an input-queue drain whose timing is a pure function of kernel order, a fairness gate that floors damage at the moment it is applied, a keyed and namespaced RNG, dormant sections that cost nothing and are re-based on load, an eager-plus-guarded topology refresh, a restore-equivalence rule for the products that cross hooks (two narrow persisted columns), and the budgets and measurement protocol for the hooks, the snapshot and the restore.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable, mono build probed), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (simulation scheduling, integer propagation, deterministic randomness) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. Nothing here calls a post-4.3 engine API. The two 4.7 GDScript rows in `breaking-changes.md` bind it: packed-array element writes run no setter (the Graph has no setters and marks dirty keys explicitly, ADR-0011 § 10), and an override inherits a typed return (the hook callables are registered `Callable`s, not overrides, and every branch ends in `return ctx.complete()`). The engine reference has no core or scripting module (`modules/` holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering, ui), so packed-array, integer and loop-cost claims rest on ADR-0005's probe table (P1 to P22), on ADR-0011's probes and on this ADR's own probes, and stay UNVERIFIED on a release export until S1 (SP-ENG-1) and S3 run there. |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`; `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows); `deprecated-apis.md` (untyped Array/Dictionary row); `current-best-practices.md` (GDScript 4.7 rows); ADR-0005 Engine Compatibility P6 to P9, P14, P17 (cited by number); ADR-0011 Engine Compatibility (a) to (i). No `modules/*.md` applies. |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None. `mini`, `maxi`, `clampi`, `absi`, `signi` (probed to exist and return `int` by ADR-0011), `posmod`, `PackedInt64Array`/`PackedInt32Array`/`PackedByteArray` element reads and writes, `fill`, and `Callable.call` with a fixed argument list. |
| **Verification Required** | Probed 2026-10-29 on `Godot_v4.7.2-stable_mono_win64_console.exe --headless --script` (editor binary, not a release export; script in `C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/adr-probes/0012/probe.gd`): **(a)** the namespaced RNG counter `(step_no << 20) \| (kind << 18) \| id` differs between node 5 and edge 5 at the same step (129,452,998,661 versus 129,453,260,805 at `step_no` 123,456), which the GDD's un-namespaced `(step_no << 20) \| subject_id` cannot do (ADR-0011 Risk 7); **(b)** `raw & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` is non-negative for the signed constant `-7046029254386353131` and for `-1` (9,223,372,036,854,775,807), and `posmod` of the masked value by 1000 returns 677, so the burst test needs no float and no `%`; **(c)** an insertion sort of packed `(key << 8) \| arrival` entries over a `PackedInt64Array` costs 4.0 microseconds for 16 entries, 32.8 for 56 and 42.9 for 64 (each figure includes refilling the array, editor binary), the bound for the queue drains of § 5; **(d)** a read-modify-write loop over 4,096 elements costs 51.6 microseconds direct and 73.4 through an `int32` active-list indirection (about 5 nanoseconds per element extra), the price of the dormant-skipping lists of § 10; **(e)** per-element delta accumulate, apply and re-zero over 4,096 elements costs 134.5 microseconds against 69.5 for `duplicate()` plus a rewrite plus a swap by reference (the dense full-column case; the Graph's Jacobi columns are the compartment rows, 14 at MVP and about 120 in VS-A, so neither dominates, and § 3 chooses accumulators for reasons of conservation and sparsity, not speed); **(f)** `clampi` inside that loop adds about 17 microseconds per 4,096 calls (about 4 nanoseconds per call). **Still open and named:** S1 (SP-ENG-1: a stub Graph with 12 phases on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release exports, accessor and `Callable.call` overhead per ms, `IntMath.floor_div` cost in the real phases) gates acceptance of every budget in § 13; S3 (snapshot, restore and `post_restore` time and size on the F-MVP fixture); KRN-LAT-02 for whether `ClockView.tick()` inside P3 names the executing tick or the next one (§ 1 makes `step_no` insensitive to it for offsets up to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 2`); S0-a/S0-b on a `template_release` export for the aliasing and integer behaviour this ADR relies on through ADR-0011. |

## ADR Dependencies

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Depends On** | ADR-0011 (tables, columns, `GraphScratch`, `GraphCaches`, descriptor store, queues, value types, fault domain 3; Proposed), ADR-0003 (`HookDescriptor`, `after` edges with `tolerates_stale`, `WriteScope` phases, mutator status contract, hook schedule compiled from `T mod C`, `STEP_BUDGET_MS` as an alarm; Proposed), ADR-0004 (dirty-key marks, dedupe, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` collapse, quiet writes; Proposed), ADR-0005 (`RngFacet.draw`, plain streams, `IntMath`, integer-only contract; Proposed), ADR-0001 (P0 to P6 tick phases, the executing tick `T`; Proposed), ADR-0006 (restore contract, snapshot hitch; Proposed), ADR-0007 (`GraphTuning`, boot tiers; Proposed), ADR-0010 (`## @hot`, HOT-01, CNT-01 to CNT-04, `WorkCounter`, ladder rungs, lint rules; Proposed). None is Accepted, so this ADR cannot be Accepted before them. |
| **Enables** | ADR-0021 (weld, cut and install transaction: calls `can_join`, `weld_join`, `cut_detach` and `ensure_derived` as defined in § 4, § 6 and § 9), ADR-0016 (hook cursor verifier, restore ordering), ADR-0017 (Emitter State reads `served_pm` and `failures()` and deposits `M14` on the § 5 schedule), ADR-0022 (Attention: `alarm_sections()`, `M17` STRESS, exogenous cause), ADR-0026 (Web Map: `M19` and dormant semantics), ADR-0027 (Suit: `M15`/`M16` timing and the grant), ADR-0028 (lamp brightness from `served_pm`), ADR-0031 (Debug Overlay: per-phase work counters). |
| **Blocks** | The Graph epic's propagation stories (every phase, the fairness gate, cascades, thaw rolls, dormant re-basing), the S1 benchmark harness story, the D.15 fixture stories (TR-derelict-012) and the restore-equivalence test story. Stories citing this ADR stay Blocked while it is Proposed. |
| **Ordering Note** | Write `graph_rules.gd` additions (`gas_flux`, `gate_floor`, `rng_subject`, `onset_valid`) and their unit tests first: ADR-0007's loader and the Item DB lints call the pure rules before any kernel exists. Land the S1 stub Graph (12 empty phases, the real active lists and accumulators) before the phase bodies, because it decides which budget lever is taken. The three ADR-0010 lint additions of Foundation Asks 2 and 3 should land with the first `propagate/` file. |

## Context

### Problem Statement

ADR-0011 fixed *what the Graph stores*. It left to this ADR *how the stored state advances*: which hooks, which phases in which order, how a phase may read and write so that one pass is order-independent and conserves, when queued inputs take effect, how the fairness gate is enforced, how randomness is keyed, what a dormant section costs, when topology is rebuilt, and which budgets the whole thing must meet and how they are measured. The GDD (LS-8) specifies the twelve phases and the staggered hooks in prose and defers the "explicit one-pass propagation scheme" to ADR-LSG-03. The Foundation ADRs have since made decisions the GDD could not know: hooks are `Callable`s registered with `after` edges that are validated and sorted once, a hook receives a `WriteScope` and a `HookContext` and ends in `return ctx.complete()`, `HookDescriptor` has no `before` edge, division goes only through `IntMath`, a faulted scope closes, zero-allocation claims are restated as `HOT-01` plus object-count checks, and the kernel snapshot may be taken on any tick.

The review of the GDD against those decisions also found four points the GDD gets wrong or leaves open, and this ADR must settle each rather than repeat them: **(1)** LS-1 (j) and ADR-0011 § 6.2 describe the Jacobi snapshot as a `next` column swapped by reference, which fits a dense per-element rewrite but not the pairwise fluxes of the exchange phases; **(2)** LS-9's `subject_id < 2^20` key is shared by node ids and edge ids, which overlap numerically (ADR-0011 Risk 7); **(3)** LS-21 says `served_pm` is not persisted "because phase 2 recomputes it before use", but three hooks and other blocks' hooks read it afterwards, and `post_restore` cannot reproduce it from the post-phase state (the battery has been debited, the room temperature has moved and a cable may have failed since), so a restored run would diverge from the uninterrupted one; **(4)** LS-17's M19 advances five kinds of absolute step stamp on load but omits two (`thaw_until`, a LOAD's `energised_at`), so a thaw window or an inrush window would be spent while the section slept.

### Constraints

- **Kernel (ADR-0001, ADR-0003):** a hook runs when `T mod divisor == offset`, in a total order built once from `after` edges and registration index; `after` edges between hooks that do not always co-run must declare `tolerates_stale`; P2 (apply) precedes P3 (hooks) inside a tick; a hook ends in `return ctx.complete()`; the first fault closes the scope; the snapshot is taken at a tick boundary after P5, on any tick; P3 target is 2.0 ms P99 with `STEP_BUDGET_MS` an alarm, never a cut-off. `HookDescriptor.after` is the only ordering primitive (no `before`).
- **Determinism (ADR-0005):** integer-only; ascending-id iteration; no Dictionary iteration; no `sort_custom`; keyed RNG through `RngFacet.draw` with a plain stream for everything the Graph draws, never reading `restore_epoch`; every division through `IntMath`; every intermediate below 2^62 (ADR-0011 § 2.3, GDD D.13).
- **Data model (ADR-0011):** the columns, the four classes, the tombstone and canonical-zero rules, `GraphScratch` for "the accumulators and flux arrays ADR-0012 declares", the descriptor store built once in phase 11, the queue tables and their bounds, the fault domain 3 list, and the writer-file rule (OWN-01).
- **Source rules (ADR-0010):** `:=` banned and every `var` explicitly typed; `## @hot` functions free of allocation tokens (`.new(`, `.duplicate(`, `.resize(`, `.append_array(`, string building, lambdas); no `await`; no recursion or iterate-to-convergence loop (GDD AC, lint requested in Foundation Ask 3); work counted through an injected `WorkCounter`, never by wall clock.
- **Capacity and bounds (registry, cited by name):** `MAX_GRAPH_NODES`, `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES`, `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION`, `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP`, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`, `MAX_CREW`, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (derived `W_MIN_STEPS`), `THAW_ROLL_STEPS`, `BURST_P_PM`, `BURST_HP_TO`, `DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION`, `GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS`. Never retyped here.
- **Performance (R12):** every wall-clock figure is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; the per-commit gates are deterministic counts.

### Requirements

- Three chained hooks at `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, twelve fixed phases, `step_no = floor(T / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)` for all three, per-hook persisted cursors (TR-lsg-008, TR-lsg-009).
- One pass per loop, order-independent within a phase, no solver, no catch-up (TR-lsg-007), with the equalisation flux stable by construction (TR-lsg-032).
- One idempotent topology refresh that no hook ever reads half-applied (TR-lsg-010, TR-assembly-034).
- Keyed, restore-independent randomness and a persisted thaw window (TR-lsg-011, TR-lsg-012).
- The fairness gate as a sim rule with an exogenous bypass and a pure `alarm_sections()` (TR-lsg-013, TR-lsg-015).
- The mutator contract M1 to M19 and the three input queues with a deterministic drain schedule (TR-lsg-016, 017, 035, TR-suit-039).
- Weld, cut and discard data effects that only append or tombstone (TR-lsg-027, 028, TR-boarding-039, 041).
- Dormant sections skipped, frozen and re-based (TR-lsg-029, TR-webmap-041, TR-ftrail-038).
- Endogenous rates, derelict compression and the eight D.15 fault fixtures (TR-derelict-011, 012, 037).
- Hook, snapshot and restore budgets with a measurement protocol and work bounded by construction (TR-lsg-025, 026, 036, TR-interact-038).

## Decision

### 1. One step, three hooks, three cursors (TR-lsg-008)

A **step** is the unit of Graph time. `step_no = IntMath.floor_div(clock.tick(), tuning.graph_step_ticks)` for all three hooks (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, the same constant as the hooks' divisor). The three hooks of step *n* run on ticks `6n + o_power`, `6n + o_atmo` and `6n + o_failure` with the offsets 0, 2 and 4. The offsets are data in `GraphTuning` (`hook_offset_power`, `hook_offset_atmo`, `hook_offset_failure`), so the GDD's data-only revert (all three 0) is a data change. A boot check (`GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING`, ADR-0011 § 8.4) requires the offsets to be non-decreasing and each at most `graph_step_ticks - 2`; the second rule makes `step_no` identical whether `ClockView.tick()` inside P3 names the executing tick or the next one (KRN-LAT-02 has not yet said which), because `floor_div(6n + o + 1, 6)` equals `n` for every `o <= 4`.

| Hook id | Offset | `after` | Phases | Cursor written at the end |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `graph.propagate.power` | `hook_offset_power` (0) | none | 0 to 3 | `last_step_power` |
| `graph.propagate.atmo` | `hook_offset_atmo` (2) | `{id: graph.propagate.power, tolerates_stale: true}` | 4 to 7 | `last_step_atmo` |
| `graph.propagate.failure` | `hook_offset_failure` (4) | `{id: graph.propagate.atmo, tolerates_stale: true}` | 8 to 11 | `last_step_failure` and `last_step_no` |

The two edges fix the resolved order (power, then atmo, then failure) even though the hooks never run on one tick at the baseline offsets; `tolerates_stale` is declared on both so the kernel's boot warning list stays empty (ADR-0003 § 8 check 3). The Graph registers the three descriptors consecutively, power first, so registration index agrees with the edges. Dependents name the hook they read: Suit's `suit.vitals` is `after: graph.propagate.atmo` at the same offset, Attention is `after: graph.propagate.power`, Emitter State's `emitter.place` is `after: graph.propagate.failure` (all registered by their owners, architecture hook schedule).

**Cursor semantics.** `last_step_X` is the `step_no` of the last completed run of hook X. `last_step_no` is the last **complete** step, written by the failure hook at its end. This is the GDD's definition (LS-8); ADR-0011 § 2.3 words it as "the last step whose power hook completed", which is a different number for ticks 6n+0 to 6n+3, and this ADR sides with the GDD because the readers that compare it (Failure & Trail's poll cache, FT-15) want a step whose descriptors have been emitted (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011). A run applies a guard before any write: `step_no < last_step_X`, or `step_no == last_step_X` with `step_no > 0`, is a defect (the clock moved backwards or the hook ran twice) and raises `GraphFaults.HOOK_CURSOR` (a new local code, cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011 § 8.1). Step 0 is the one exception, because a fresh block holds all cursors at 0 and cannot tell "step 0 not yet run" from "step 0 done". A step that did not happen (the kernel never drops a tick at `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` 0, and a longer stall delays ticks without skipping them) leaves a gap between cursors and is **not** repaired: the Graph never catches up and never runs a step twice (TR-lsg-007).

**The hook skeleton** (the same for all three; `hook_power` shown):

```gdscript
# src/sim/graph/graph_module.gd (additions; ADR-0011 § Key Interfaces holds the rest)
func hook_power(views: SimViews, scope: WriteScope, ctx: HookContext) -> CompletionToken:
	if not scope.open_for(GraphModule.BLOCK_ID):
		return ctx.complete()                                  # REFUSED: the kernel counts it; nothing written
	var step_no: int = IntMath.floor_div(_clock.tick(), _tuning.graph_step_ticks)
	if GraphPropagate.enter(scope, _state, _caches, _diag, GraphPropagate.HOOK_POWER, step_no) != MutatorStatus.OK:
		return ctx.complete()                                  # cursor defect: scope already faulted
	GraphPropagate.run_power(_state, _caches, _scratch, _diag, _tuning, step_no, scope, _work)
	return ctx.complete()
```

`GraphPropagate.enter` performs the cursor guard, the head-of-hook topology guard (§ 4) and nothing else; `run_power` runs phases 0 to 3 and, after each phase, returns early if `scope.faulted` (a structural fault closes the scope, ADR-0003 § 5, and the partial writes stay for the diagnostic dump); the last statement of `run_*` writes the cursor. A hook never reads a wall clock, never calls another owner's mutator, never submits a command and never allocates in steady state.

An EMPTY block (no sections instantiated, or `default_state`) runs the hooks over empty active lists: they cost nothing and the cursors still advance, so a later `INIT` or restore finds them consistent with `T`.

### 2. The twelve phases (TR-lsg-009)

The order is fixed and is the same on every run. Each phase is one `## @hot` static function in `src/sim/graph/propagate/` taking its collaborators as arguments (no member access through a hidden `self`), so a phase can alias a column in a local for the length of the phase (ADR-0011 § 6.2 rule 1).

| # | Hook | Phase | Reads | Writes | Write discipline (§ 3) | Keys fired (§ 12) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | power | **Inputs.** (a) stock reconcile (ADR-0011 § 7.3); (b) drain `pending_load`, `pending_draw`, `pending_trace` (§ 5); (c) apply `forced_next` to `forced_mode` | queues, stores, `forced_next` | `stock`, `req`, `n_o2`, `hp`, `hp_cap`, flags, `forced_mode`, `draw_grant`, section counters | OWN; ALLOC for draws | none (marked in 11) |
| 1 | power | **Topology guard.** No-op while `topo_dirty` is clear (§ 4) | edges, flags | caches only | none | none |
| 2 | power | **POWER solve per island** (D.6): reactor ramp, thermostat scaling, inrush, tiers, battery flow, merit-order dispatch, edge net flow | `req`, `out_w`, `stock`, breakers, topology | `out_w`, `stock`, `n_served`, `e_load`, `produced_dj`, power summary | ALLOC per island | `LOOP` (power) |
| 3 | power | **FUEL** (D.2 family): burn, `fuel_rem`, transfer tank to burner, `starve_steps` | stocks, `out_w`, `path_cap` | `stock`, `fuel_rem`, `burned_uml`, `starve_steps` | ALLOC per component | `LOOP` (fuel) |
| 4 | atmo | **O2** (D.5, D.2): scrubber output, vent injection, duct and tank leaks | `n_served`, pool, compartments | tank `stock`, `acc_n_o2`, `acc_n_inert`, `vented_mgu`, `breathed`/`produced` counters | ALLOC (pool), JAC (rooms) | `LOOP` (O2) |
| 5 | atmo | **COOLANT** (D.8): `circ`, capture, radiator, `t_cool`, pipe and reservoir leaks | `n_served`, reservoirs, `t` | `stock`, `t_cool`, `tc_rem`, `spilled_*`, `acc_q` | ALLOC (reservoir), OWN, JAC (heat) | `LOOP` (coolant) |
| 6 | atmo | **Atmosphere exchange** (D.1, D.2): stored OPENINGs, virtual holes, seam weeps | `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `V` | `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `vented_mgu` (apply `acc_n_*`) | **JAC** | none (marked in 7) |
| 7 | atmo | **Thermal step and close-out** (D.7, D.3): conduction, hull loss, machine and heater input, remainder carry; then intensive recompute, bands, pressure trend | `t`, `t_rem`, `acc_q` | `t`, `t_rem`, `radiated_dj`, `band_*`, `p_prev`; caches `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, trend | **JAC**, then OWN | `COMP`, `BAND` |
| 8 | failure | **Damage** (D.9): overload, wear, duty, short burn, thaw rolls, patch decay, with the fairness floor | `e_load`, `n_served`, modes, flags, `thaw_until` | `hp`, `thaw_until`, EXOGENOUS flag, `GraphDiag.gate_holds` | OWN | none (marked in 11) |
| 9 | failure | **State evaluation:** `state`, mode triggers and pre-stages, `warn_since`, `fail_since`, `sev`, onsets, compartment warn trackers | `hp`, `t`, bands, `n_served` | `state`, `forced_mode` (own row), `mode_key`, `mode_since`, `isolated_at`, `warn_*`, `fail_since`, flags, `thaw_until` | OWN | `NODE`, `EDGE`, `SEAM` |
| 10 | failure | **Cascades:** cross-subject rules on this run's phase-9 states, admitted in ascending subject id up to `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP` | phase-9 states | `forced_next` | ALLOC (the spread budget) | none |
| 11 | failure | **Emit:** descriptor store, alarm list, `hp` and store and intensity buckets, loop summaries not yet marked, `last_step_no` | everything | `GraphCaches` only; the cursor | none | `NODE`/`EDGE` (hp, store buckets), `DESC` |

Notes on the table, each a decision:

- **Phase 0 is first because it is the only place where the inputs of the whole world are folded in.** The three queues are the unconditional channels (kernel CR-9 path (a)); folding them in at one point makes every Graph result a function of the persisted state at the start of the step, which is what lets a snapshot taken on any tick be replayed (§ 11).
- **Phase 1 is a guard, not work** (§ 4). The GDD runs the topology refresh "at the head of whichever Graph hook first runs after a structural mutator"; here that head is `GraphPropagate.enter` for all three hooks, and phase 1 of the power hook is the same guard retained for the numbering the consumers (Debug Overlay, GDD) know.
- **Phase 6 applies phase 4's buffered gas deltas and phase 5's buffered heat is applied in phase 7**, so both exchange phases read the start-of-run amounts (nothing writes `n_o2`, `n_inert` or `t` between the start of phase 4 and the apply in phase 6, and nothing writes `t` between the start of phase 5 and the apply in phase 7). The O2 and coolant phases therefore need no snapshot copy: the live column *is* the start-of-phase snapshot until the apply.
- **Phase 9 evaluates a subject's own triggers; phase 10 evaluates cross-subject chains.** A subject's own row may take a forced mode in phase 9 (FREEZE once the gate is open; SCRAM after sustained OVERHEAT or fuel starve), gated by § 7. A chain whose trigger is subject A's state and whose effect lands on subject B (LS-12) queues B's `forced_next` in phase 10, and phase 0 of the *next* step applies it: one hop per step, never an instant cascade. A candidate that does not fit the spread budget is not stored: its trigger condition still holds, so phase 10 proposes it again next run, and the finite subject count bounds the wait.
- **Phase 11's "block_hash dirty flag" row of the GDD is obsolete.** The kernel invalidates the cached hash by the touch serial of every granted `open_for` (ADR-0005 § 5.2), so the Graph does nothing. This is a `gdd_sync` item.
- **Atmosphere bands and the intensive caches are closed out at the end of phase 7**, the last writer of `n_o2`, `n_inert` and `t` in a step. Phase 0's `draw_air` debits `n_o2` two ticks before that, so `P` and `p_o2` can lag the breath by up to two ticks; they are quantised display and band inputs, never a flux input (D.1), and the lag is below any consumer's resolution.

### 3. One pass: three write disciplines (TR-lsg-007, TR-lsg-032)

A **pass** is one traversal in ascending slot order over a loop's active list in which no element reads a value written by another element of the same phase. The GDD's phrase "Jacobi from a double-buffered start-of-phase snapshot" is made exact by three disciplines, and every column a phase writes is declared with one of them in the phase's doc comment (a reviewer and a test can check the declaration against the code):

- **JAC (Jacobi).** Every element reads only start-of-phase values and writes only into a `GraphScratch` accumulator; the accumulators are applied to the live column in one ascending loop at the end of the phase (`col[i] += acc[i]; acc[i] = 0`). Used by the gas exchange (phase 6 plus phase 4's room deltas), the heat input (phases 5 and 7). Because the live column is untouched until the apply, it *is* the start-of-phase snapshot, so there is no copy and no swap.
- **ALLOC (ordered allocation).** A shared quantity (an island's supply, a tank pool, a reservoir's level, the spread budget) is allocated to claimants in ascending id order against a running balance; each claimant reads only the balance and its own row. Used by the power solve, fuel, the O2 pool, reservoir leaks, the draw queue and cascades. This is a single sequential pass, not iteration.
- **OWN (own-row).** An element reads and writes only its own row and values no other element writes in the phase. Used by damage, state evaluation, `t_cool`, queue application to a named subject.

**Why accumulators, not `next` columns (a refinement of ADR-0011 § 6.2 (4) and LS-1 (j)).** A `next` column per field needs a full copy before the pass (every untouched row must be carried over) and a swap after; probe (e) shows the dense case costs about half of the accumulate-and-apply form, so speed does not decide it. Three other things do. The exchange flux is pairwise (one `Δn` is subtracted from one room and added to another), so an accumulator makes conservation visible in one place: the sum of the accumulator is zero by construction apart from the `vented` term, and a test asserts it per run. The accumulator form touches only the rows with a flux, which keeps VS-A quiescence (a section with every flux zero) a pure skip. And the persisted column is never aliased across a kernel call, so no snapshot can capture a half-swapped column. The swap-by-reference rule of ADR-0011 stays available for any future field that is rewritten wholesale; none exists at MVP, so `GraphScratch` holds accumulators only (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011 § 6.2).

**The scratch inventory** (all `GraphScratch`, sized by `GraphCaches.size_scratch()` in every structural mutator and in `post_restore`, never in a phase; each is all-zero at every hook exit, asserted in tests):

| Member | Type | Rows | Phase (fill / apply) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acc_n_o2`, `acc_n_inert` | `PackedInt64Array` | compartments | 4, 6 / 6 |
| `acc_q` | `PackedInt64Array` | compartments (dJ) | 5, 7 / 7 |
| `acc_vent_mgu` | `PackedInt64Array` | sections | 6 / 6 (folded into `vented_mgu` at the apply) |
| `island_*` (supply, demand, battery draw, charge, root) | `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedInt64Array` | power components | 2 |
| `cand_slot`, `cand_mode` | `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedByteArray` | nodes + edges (candidate list) | 9 / 10 |
| `q_key` | `PackedInt64Array` | longest queue | 0 (drain sort) |
| `stack`, `queue` | `PackedInt32Array` | nodes (iterative traversals, § 4) | 1 |

**The equalisation flux (TR-lsg-032).** The gas flux across one opening is the D.1 formula and nothing else; it is a pure function in `graph_rules.gd` so the Item DB lints, `can_join` and the phase call the same code:

```gdscript
# src/shared/graph/graph_rules.gd
## @hot  Magnitude of the D.1 flux across one opening; the caller takes the direction from the sign of g = n_a*v_b - n_b*v_a.
static func gas_flux(g_abs: int, v_a: int, v_b: int, a_m: int, deg_max: int, g_open: int, gas_scale: int) -> int:
	var first: int = IntMath.floor_div(g_open * a_m * g_abs, v_a * v_b * gas_scale * 1000)
	var second: int = IntMath.floor_div(g_abs, (v_a + v_b) * deg_max)
	return mini(first, second)
```

The gradient `g` uses the exact integer amounts at the start of the phase, never the floored display pressures, so a floor can neither reverse a flux near balance nor break monotonicity. The product `g_open * a_m * g_abs` is on the D.13 product list (worst case about 3 x 10^17, under 2^62). The stability argument (D.12): the second term caps one edge at `|g| / ((V_a + V_b) x deg_max)`, which removes at most `1/deg_max` of the gradient across that edge; with `Σ k <= 10^6` per room (asserted at boot over every template room and by `can_join` for both seam rooms, reason `STABILITY`) the update is a convex combination, so the maximum `|ΔP|` over all open edges is non-increasing and no edge's flux direction alternates from one run to the next. The thermal analogue is the second sum of D.12 and is enforced the same way. This ADR does not re-derive D.12; it fixes that the property is a **test**, not an argument: the S1 sealed stability fixture (a room of degree 4 or more at 1010 dkPa among rooms at 200) asserts non-increasing `max |ΔP|` and no direction flip every run until quiescence, on every commit that touches `propagate/` (§ Validation).

**No iteration to convergence, no recursion, no catch-up.** No phase contains a loop whose bound is a convergence condition; every loop is bounded by an active-list count, a table row count or a literal constant (the insertion sort of § 5 is a bounded `for` with `break`). No function is recursive. The Graph never runs a step twice and never runs a missed step (§ 1). Foundation Ask 3 asks for the lint (`PROP-01`) that enforces the first two.

Proposed

Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.

## Summary
The Life-Support Graph must advance five coupled loops (power, fuel, oxygen, coolant, gas and heat exchange) and the failure lifecycle deterministically, inside a spike share of the kernel's P3 budget, and must survive a snapshot taken on any tick. This ADR fixes the propagation scheme: one logical step of twelve fixed phases split across three chained step hooks at divisor `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` (offsets 0, 2, 4), exactly one pass per loop per step with three declared write disciplines (delta accumulators, ordered allocation, own-row), an input-queue drain whose timing is a pure function of kernel order, a fairness gate that floors damage at the moment it is applied, a keyed and namespaced RNG, dormant sections that cost nothing and are re-based on load, an eager-plus-guarded topology refresh, a restore-equivalence rule for the products that cross hooks (two narrow persisted columns), and the budgets and measurement protocol for the hooks, the snapshot and the restore.

## Context

### Problem Statement

ADR-0011 fixed *what the Graph stores*. It left to this ADR *how the stored state advances*: which hooks, which phases in which order, how a phase may read and write so that one pass is order-independent and conserves, when queued inputs take effect, how the fairness gate is enforced, how randomness is keyed, what a dormant section costs, when topology is rebuilt, and which budgets the whole thing must meet and how they are measured. The GDD (LS-8) specifies the twelve phases and the staggered hooks in prose and defers the "explicit one-pass propagation scheme" to ADR-LSG-03. The Foundation ADRs have since made decisions the GDD could not know: hooks are `Callable`s registered with `after` edges that are validated and sorted once, a hook receives a `WriteScope` and a `HookContext` and ends in `return ctx.complete()`, `HookDescriptor` has no `before` edge, division goes only through `IntMath`, a faulted scope closes, zero-allocation claims are restated as `HOT-01` plus object-count checks, and the kernel snapshot may be taken on any tick.

The review of the GDD against those decisions also found four points the GDD gets wrong or leaves open, and this ADR must settle each rather than repeat them: **(1)** LS-1 (j) and ADR-0011 § 6.2 describe the Jacobi snapshot as a `next` column swapped by reference, which fits a dense per-element rewrite but not the pairwise fluxes of the exchange phases; **(2)** LS-9's `subject_id < 2^20` key is shared by node ids and edge ids, which overlap numerically (ADR-0011 Risk 7); **(3)** LS-21 says `served_pm` is not persisted "because phase 2 recomputes it before use", but three hooks and other blocks' hooks read it afterwards, and `post_restore` cannot reproduce it from the post-phase state (the battery has been debited, the room temperature has moved and a cable may have failed since), so a restored run would diverge from the uninterrupted one; **(4)** LS-17's M19 advances five kinds of absolute step stamp on load but omits two (`thaw_until`, a LOAD's `energised_at`), so a thaw window or an inrush window would be spent while the section slept.

### Constraints

- **Kernel (ADR-0001, ADR-0003):** a hook runs when `T mod divisor == offset`, in a total order built once from `after` edges and registration index; `after` edges between hooks that do not always co-run must declare `tolerates_stale`; P2 (apply) precedes P3 (hooks) inside a tick; a hook ends in `return ctx.complete()`; the first fault closes the scope; the snapshot is taken at a tick boundary after P5, on any tick; P3 target is 2.0 ms P99 with `STEP_BUDGET_MS` an alarm, never a cut-off. `HookDescriptor.after` is the only ordering primitive (no `before`).
- **Determinism (ADR-0005):** integer-only; ascending-id iteration; no Dictionary iteration; no `sort_custom`; keyed RNG through `RngFacet.draw` with a plain stream for everything the Graph draws, never reading `restore_epoch`; every division through `IntMath`; every intermediate below 2^62 (ADR-0011 § 2.3, GDD D.13).
- **Data model (ADR-0011):** the columns, the four classes, the tombstone and canonical-zero rules, `GraphScratch` for "the accumulators and flux arrays ADR-0012 declares", the descriptor store built once in phase 11, the queue tables and their bounds, the fault domain 3 list, and the writer-file rule (OWN-01).
- **Source rules (ADR-0010):** `:=` banned and every `var` explicitly typed; `## @hot` functions free of allocation tokens (`.new(`, `.duplicate(`, `.resize(`, `.append_array(`, string building, lambdas); no `await`; no recursion or iterate-to-convergence loop (GDD AC, lint requested in Foundation Ask 3); work counted through an injected `WorkCounter`, never by wall clock.
- **Capacity and bounds (registry, cited by name):** `MAX_GRAPH_NODES`, `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES`, `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION`, `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP`, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`, `MAX_CREW`, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (derived `W_MIN_STEPS`), `THAW_ROLL_STEPS`, `BURST_P_PM`, `BURST_HP_TO`, `DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION`, `GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS`. Never retyped here.
- **Performance (R12):** every wall-clock figure is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; the per-commit gates are deterministic counts.

### Requirements

- Three chained hooks at `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, twelve fixed phases, `step_no = floor(T / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)` for all three, per-hook persisted cursors (TR-lsg-008, TR-lsg-009).
- One pass per loop, order-independent within a phase, no solver, no catch-up (TR-lsg-007), with the equalisation flux stable by construction (TR-lsg-032).
- One idempotent topology refresh that no hook ever reads half-applied (TR-lsg-010, TR-assembly-034).
- Keyed, restore-independent randomness and a persisted thaw window (TR-lsg-011, TR-lsg-012).
- The fairness gate as a sim rule with an exogenous bypass and a pure `alarm_sections()` (TR-lsg-013, TR-lsg-015).
- The mutator contract M1 to M19 and the three input queues with a deterministic drain schedule (TR-lsg-016, 017, 035, TR-suit-039).
- Weld, cut and discard data effects that only append or tombstone (TR-lsg-027, 028, TR-boarding-039, 041).
- Dormant sections skipped, frozen and re-based (TR-lsg-029, TR-webmap-041, TR-ftrail-038).
- Endogenous rates, derelict compression and the eight D.15 fault fixtures (TR-derelict-011, 012, 037).
- Hook, snapshot and restore budgets with a measurement protocol and work bounded by construction (TR-lsg-025, 026, 036, TR-interact-038).

## Decision

### 1. One step, three hooks, three cursors (TR-lsg-008)

A **step** is the unit of Graph time. `step_no = IntMath.floor_div(clock.tick(), tuning.graph_step_ticks)` for all three hooks (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, the same constant as the hooks' divisor). The three hooks of step *n* run on ticks `6n + o_power`, `6n + o_atmo` and `6n + o_failure` with the offsets 0, 2 and 4. The offsets are data in `GraphTuning` (`hook_offset_power`, `hook_offset_atmo`, `hook_offset_failure`), so the GDD's data-only revert (all three 0) is a data change. A boot check (`GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING`, ADR-0011 § 8.4) requires the offsets to be non-decreasing and each at most `graph_step_ticks - 2`; the second rule makes `step_no` identical whether `ClockView.tick()` inside P3 names the executing tick or the next one (KRN-LAT-02 has not yet said which), because `floor_div(6n + o + 1, 6)` equals `n` for every `o <= 4`.

| Hook id | Offset | `after` | Phases | Cursor written at the end |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `graph.propagate.power` | `hook_offset_power` (0) | none | 0 to 3 | `last_step_power` |
| `graph.propagate.atmo` | `hook_offset_atmo` (2) | `{id: graph.propagate.power, tolerates_stale: true}` | 4 to 7 | `last_step_atmo` |
| `graph.propagate.failure` | `hook_offset_failure` (4) | `{id: graph.propagate.atmo, tolerates_stale: true}` | 8 to 11 | `last_step_failure` and `last_step_no` |

The two edges fix the resolved order (power, then atmo, then failure) even though the hooks never run on one tick at the baseline offsets; `tolerates_stale` is declared on both so the kernel's boot warning list stays empty (ADR-0003 § 8 check 3). The Graph registers the three descriptors consecutively, power first, so registration index agrees with the edges. Dependents name the hook they read: Suit's `suit.vitals` is `after: graph.propagate.atmo` at the same offset, Attention is `after: graph.propagate.power`, Emitter State's `emitter.place` is `after: graph.propagate.failure` (all registered by their owners, architecture hook schedule).

**Cursor semantics.** `last_step_X` is the `step_no` of the last completed run of hook X. `last_step_no` is the last **complete** step, written by the failure hook at its end. This is the GDD's definition (LS-8); ADR-0011 § 2.3 words it as "the last step whose power hook completed", which is a different number for ticks 6n+0 to 6n+3, and this ADR sides with the GDD because the readers that compare it (Failure & Trail's poll cache, FT-15) want a step whose descriptors have been emitted (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011). A run applies a guard before any write: `step_no < last_step_X`, or `step_no == last_step_X` with `step_no > 0`, is a defect (the clock moved backwards or the hook ran twice) and raises `GraphFaults.HOOK_CURSOR` (a new local code, cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011 § 8.1). Step 0 is the one exception, because a fresh block holds all cursors at 0 and cannot tell "step 0 not yet run" from "step 0 done". A step that did not happen (the kernel never drops a tick at `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` 0, and a longer stall delays ticks without skipping them) leaves a gap between cursors and is **not** repaired: the Graph never catches up and never runs a step twice (TR-lsg-007).

**The hook skeleton** (the same for all three; `hook_power` shown):

```gdscript
# src/sim/graph/graph_module.gd (additions; ADR-0011 § Key Interfaces holds the rest)
func hook_power(views: SimViews, scope: WriteScope, ctx: HookContext) -> CompletionToken:
	if not scope.open_for(GraphModule.BLOCK_ID):
		return ctx.complete()                                  # REFUSED: the kernel counts it; nothing written
	var step_no: int = IntMath.floor_div(_clock.tick(), _tuning.graph_step_ticks)
	if GraphPropagate.enter(scope, _state, _caches, _diag, GraphPropagate.HOOK_POWER, step_no) != MutatorStatus.OK:
		return ctx.complete()                                  # cursor defect: scope already faulted
	GraphPropagate.run_power(_state, _caches, _scratch, _diag, _tuning, step_no, scope, _work)
	return ctx.complete()
```

`GraphPropagate.enter` performs the cursor guard, the head-of-hook topology guard (§ 4) and nothing else; `run_power` runs phases 0 to 3 and, after each phase, returns early if `scope.faulted` (a structural fault closes the scope, ADR-0003 § 5, and the partial writes stay for the diagnostic dump); the last statement of `run_*` writes the cursor. A hook never reads a wall clock, never calls another owner's mutator, never submits a command and never allocates in steady state.

An EMPTY block (no sections instantiated, or `default_state`) runs the hooks over empty active lists: they cost nothing and the cursors still advance, so a later `INIT` or restore finds them consistent with `T`.

### 2. The twelve phases (TR-lsg-009)

The order is fixed and is the same on every run. Each phase is one `## @hot` static function in `src/sim/graph/propagate/` taking its collaborators as arguments (no member access through a hidden `self`), so a phase can alias a column in a local for the length of the phase (ADR-0011 § 6.2 rule 1).

| # | Hook | Phase | Reads | Writes | Write discipline (§ 3) | Keys fired (§ 12) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | power | **Inputs.** (a) stock reconcile (ADR-0011 § 7.3); (b) drain `pending_load`, `pending_draw`, `pending_trace` (§ 5); (c) apply `forced_next` to `forced_mode` | queues, stores, `forced_next` | `stock`, `req`, `n_o2`, `hp`, `hp_cap`, flags, `forced_mode`, `draw_grant`, section counters | OWN; ALLOC for draws | none (marked in 11) |
| 1 | power | **Topology guard.** No-op while `topo_dirty` is clear (§ 4) | edges, flags | caches only | none | none |
| 2 | power | **POWER solve per island** (D.6): reactor ramp, thermostat scaling, inrush, tiers, battery flow, merit-order dispatch, edge net flow | `req`, `out_w`, `stock`, breakers, topology | `out_w`, `stock`, `n_served`, `e_load`, `produced_dj`, power summary | ALLOC per island | `LOOP` (power) |
| 3 | power | **FUEL** (D.2 family): burn, `fuel_rem`, transfer tank to burner, `starve_steps` | stocks, `out_w`, `path_cap` | `stock`, `fuel_rem`, `burned_uml`, `starve_steps` | ALLOC per component | `LOOP` (fuel) |
| 4 | atmo | **O2** (D.5, D.2): scrubber output, vent injection, duct and tank leaks | `n_served`, pool, compartments | tank `stock`, `acc_n_o2`, `acc_n_inert`, `vented_mgu`, `breathed`/`produced` counters | ALLOC (pool), JAC (rooms) | `LOOP` (O2) |
| 5 | atmo | **COOLANT** (D.8): `circ`, capture, radiator, `t_cool`, pipe and reservoir leaks | `n_served`, reservoirs, `t` | `stock`, `t_cool`, `tc_rem`, `spilled_*`, `acc_q` | ALLOC (reservoir), OWN, JAC (heat) | `LOOP` (coolant) |
| 6 | atmo | **Atmosphere exchange** (D.1, D.2): stored OPENINGs, virtual holes, seam weeps | `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `V` | `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `vented_mgu` (apply `acc_n_*`) | **JAC** | none (marked in 7) |
| 7 | atmo | **Thermal step and close-out** (D.7, D.3): conduction, hull loss, machine and heater input, remainder carry; then intensive recompute, bands, pressure trend | `t`, `t_rem`, `acc_q` | `t`, `t_rem`, `radiated_dj`, `band_*`, `p_prev`; caches `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, trend | **JAC**, then OWN | `COMP`, `BAND` |
| 8 | failure | **Damage** (D.9): overload, wear, duty, short burn, thaw rolls, patch decay, with the fairness floor | `e_load`, `n_served`, modes, flags, `thaw_until` | `hp`, `thaw_until`, EXOGENOUS flag, `GraphDiag.gate_holds` | OWN | none (marked in 11) |
| 9 | failure | **State evaluation:** `state`, mode triggers and pre-stages, `warn_since`, `fail_since`, `sev`, onsets, compartment warn trackers | `hp`, `t`, bands, `n_served` | `state`, `forced_mode` (own row), `mode_key`, `mode_since`, `isolated_at`, `warn_*`, `fail_since`, flags, `thaw_until` | OWN | `NODE`, `EDGE`, `SEAM` |
| 10 | failure | **Cascades:** cross-subject rules on this run's phase-9 states, admitted in ascending subject id up to `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP` | phase-9 states | `forced_next` | ALLOC (the spread budget) | none |
| 11 | failure | **Emit:** descriptor store, alarm list, `hp` and store and intensity buckets, loop summaries not yet marked, `last_step_no` | everything | `GraphCaches` only; the cursor | none | `NODE`/`EDGE` (hp, store buckets), `DESC` |

Notes on the table, each a decision:

- **Phase 0 is first because it is the only place where the inputs of the whole world are folded in.** The three queues are the unconditional channels (kernel CR-9 path (a)); folding them in at one point makes every Graph result a function of the persisted state at the start of the step, which is what lets a snapshot taken on any tick be replayed (§ 11).
- **Phase 1 is a guard, not work** (§ 4). The GDD runs the topology refresh "at the head of whichever Graph hook first runs after a structural mutator"; here that head is `GraphPropagate.enter` for all three hooks, and phase 1 of the power hook is the same guard retained for the numbering the consumers (Debug Overlay, GDD) know.
- **Phase 6 applies phase 4's buffered gas deltas and phase 5's buffered heat is applied in phase 7**, so both exchange phases read the start-of-run amounts (nothing writes `n_o2`, `n_inert` or `t` between the start of phase 4 and the apply in phase 6, and nothing writes `t` between the start of phase 5 and the apply in phase 7). The O2 and coolant phases therefore need no snapshot copy: the live column *is* the start-of-phase snapshot until the apply.
- **Phase 9 evaluates a subject's own triggers; phase 10 evaluates cross-subject chains.** A subject's own row may take a forced mode in phase 9 (FREEZE once the gate is open; SCRAM after sustained OVERHEAT or fuel starve), gated by § 7. A chain whose trigger is subject A's state and whose effect lands on subject B (LS-12) queues B's `forced_next` in phase 10, and phase 0 of the *next* step applies it: one hop per step, never an instant cascade. A candidate that does not fit the spread budget is not stored: its trigger condition still holds, so phase 10 proposes it again next run, and the finite subject count bounds the wait.
- **Phase 11's "block_hash dirty flag" row of the GDD is obsolete.** The kernel invalidates the cached hash by the touch serial of every granted `open_for` (ADR-0005 § 5.2), so the Graph does nothing. This is a `gdd_sync` item.
- **Atmosphere bands and the intensive caches are closed out at the end of phase 7**, the last writer of `n_o2`, `n_inert` and `t` in a step. Phase 0's `draw_air` debits `n_o2` two ticks before that, so `P` and `p_o2` can lag the breath by up to two ticks; they are quantised display and band inputs, never a flux input (D.1), and the lag is below any consumer's resolution.

### 3. One pass: three write disciplines (TR-lsg-007, TR-lsg-032)

A **pass** is one traversal in ascending slot order over a loop's active list in which no element reads a value written by another element of the same phase. The GDD's phrase "Jacobi from a double-buffered start-of-phase snapshot" is made exact by three disciplines, and every column a phase writes is declared with one of them in the phase's doc comment (a reviewer and a test can check the declaration against the code):

- **JAC (Jacobi).** Every element reads only start-of-phase values and writes only into a `GraphScratch` accumulator; the accumulators are applied to the live column in one ascending loop at the end of the phase (`col[i] += acc[i]; acc[i] = 0`). Used by the gas exchange (phase 6 plus phase 4's room deltas), the heat input (phases 5 and 7). Because the live column is untouched until the apply, it *is* the start-of-phase snapshot, so there is no copy and no swap.
- **ALLOC (ordered allocation).** A shared quantity (an island's supply, a tank pool, a reservoir's level, the spread budget) is allocated to claimants in ascending id order against a running balance; each claimant reads only the balance and its own row. Used by the power solve, fuel, the O2 pool, reservoir leaks, the draw queue and cascades. This is a single sequential pass, not iteration.
- **OWN (own-row).** An element reads and writes only its own row and values no other element writes in the phase. Used by damage, state evaluation, `t_cool`, queue application to a named subject.

**Why accumulators, not `next` columns (a refinement of ADR-0011 § 6.2 (4) and LS-1 (j)).** A `next` column per field needs a full copy before the pass (every untouched row must be carried over) and a swap after; probe (e) shows the dense case costs about half of the accumulate-and-apply form, so speed does not decide it. Three other things do. The exchange flux is pairwise (one `Δn` is subtracted from one room and added to another), so an accumulator makes conservation visible in one place: the sum of the accumulator is zero by construction apart from the `vented` term, and a test asserts it per run. The accumulator form touches only the rows with a flux, which keeps VS-A quiescence (a section with every flux zero) a pure skip. And the persisted column is never aliased across a kernel call, so no snapshot can capture a half-swapped column. The swap-by-reference rule of ADR-0011 stays available for any future field that is rewritten wholesale; none exists at MVP, so `GraphScratch` holds accumulators only (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011 § 6.2).

**The scratch inventory** (all `GraphScratch`, sized by `GraphCaches.size_scratch()` in every structural mutator and in `post_restore`, never in a phase; each is all-zero at every hook exit, asserted in tests):

| Member | Type | Rows | Phase (fill / apply) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acc_n_o2`, `acc_n_inert` | `PackedInt64Array` | compartments | 4, 6 / 6 |
| `acc_q` | `PackedInt64Array` | compartments (dJ) | 5, 7 / 7 |
| `acc_vent_mgu` | `PackedInt64Array` | sections | 6 / 6 (folded into `vented_mgu` at the apply) |
| `island_*` (supply, demand, battery draw, charge, root) | `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedInt64Array` | power components | 2 |
| `cand_slot`, `cand_mode` | `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedByteArray` | nodes + edges (candidate list) | 9 / 10 |
| `q_key` | `PackedInt64Array` | longest queue | 0 (drain sort) |
| `stack`, `queue` | `PackedInt32Array` | nodes (iterative traversals, § 4) | 1 |

**The equalisation flux (TR-lsg-032).** The gas flux across one opening is the D.1 formula and nothing else; it is a pure function in `graph_rules.gd` so the Item DB lints, `can_join` and the phase call the same code:

```gdscript
# src/shared/graph/graph_rules.gd
## @hot  Magnitude of the D.1 flux across one opening; the caller takes the direction from the sign of g = n_a*v_b - n_b*v_a.
static func gas_flux(g_abs: int, v_a: int, v_b: int, a_m: int, deg_max: int, g_open: int, gas_scale: int) -> int:
	var first: int = IntMath.floor_div(g_open * a_m * g_abs, v_a * v_b * gas_scale * 1000)
	var second: int = IntMath.floor_div(g_abs, (v_a + v_b) * deg_max)
	return mini(first, second)
```

The gradient `g` uses the exact integer amounts at the start of the phase, never the floored display pressures, so a floor can neither reverse a flux near balance nor break monotonicity. The product `g_open * a_m * g_abs` is on the D.13 product list (worst case about 3 x 10^17, under 2^62). The stability argument (D.12): the second term caps one edge at `|g| / ((V_a + V_b) x deg_max)`, which removes at most `1/deg_max` of the gradient across that edge; with `Σ k <= 10^6` per room (asserted at boot over every template room and by `can_join` for both seam rooms, reason `STABILITY`) the update is a convex combination, so the maximum `|ΔP|` over all open edges is non-increasing and no edge's flux direction alternates from one run to the next. The thermal analogue is the second sum of D.12 and is enforced the same way. This ADR does not re-derive D.12; it fixes that the property is a **test**, not an argument: the S1 sealed stability fixture (a room of degree 4 or more at 1010 dkPa among rooms at 200) asserts non-increasing `max |ΔP|` and no direction flip every run until quiescence, on every commit that touches `propagate/` (§ Validation).

**No iteration to convergence, no recursion, no catch-up.** No phase contains a loop whose bound is a convergence condition; every loop is bounded by an active-list count, a table row count or a literal constant (the insertion sort of § 5 is a bounded `for` with `break`). No function is recursive. The Graph never runs a step twice and never runs a missed step (§ 1). Foundation Ask 3 asks for the lint (`PROP-01`) that enforces the first two.

The new persisted state would be `n_served` on nodes, `e_load` on edges, with LOAD.aux_b storing heater duty — avoiding the need for a separate `n_draw` field.

Checking the storage budget: adding 4 bytes per node and per edge brings a roster of 105 nodes/150 edges to roughly 30.7 KB, leaving only about 4% headroom under the 32 KB ceiling, tighter than the 7% margin ADR-0011 cited at 29.7 KB — I need to verify whether that 32 KB figure means 32,768 or 32,000 bytes to pin down the real margin.

Then I realize there's a way to avoid adding a new column entirely: the `e0` field is only used by DUCT (length) and OPENING (area) edge types, meaning it's sitting unused for CABLE/seam edges. I could repurpose that free `e0` slot to store the load value for cable edges instead of introducing a new field.

Turning to nodes, I check whether `req`, `req_max`, `aux_a`, `aux_b` might similarly have unused slots for non-LOAD node kinds like SCRUBBER, PUMP, VENT, REACTOR, and BATTERY, since those seem to be distinct kinds rather than LOAD subtypes.

For HEATER, duty_t isn't a static field but something derived at consumption time from temperature versus setpoint, since the thermostat keeps req_w pinned at 500 even when idle, so I need to recompute wear dynamically rather than storing it alongside served.

The tricky part is that T is read at different phases (6n+2 for heat, 6n for the power draw), so the electrical and thermal evaluations may diverge slightly at thermostat switching instants — but since T itself is deterministic persisted state, this mismatch stays bounded to one step and should be acceptable.

After going back and forth, I'm settling on persisting two node columns: `n_served` (permille) and `n_draw` (delivered watts), reusing `e0` on CABLE edges for load.

With that, `served_pm` just reads directly from `n_served`, and heat input for phases 5/7 comes from flooring `n_draw × waste_permille/1000`, matching the actual electricity drawn — reactor Q_src follows the same pattern using persisted `out_w`. For HEATER duty wear, I need `run_pm` derived from the draw-to-request ratio, working through the floor-effect math to define it consistently with the duty and saturation terms.

I settle on `run_pm(HEATER) := ⌊1000 × n_draw / req⌋`, using the persisted constant req of 500, which means duty_t is no longer needed separately in the GDD sync, while other consumers keep run_pm = n_served when req>0. The size cost is 8 bytes per node across 105 nodes, adding 840 B for a total of 30.5 KB, leaving about 4.6% headroom.

I'm now checking whether n_draw matters beyond heater waste heat — pumps, scrubbers, and lamps all produce waste heat proportional to delivered power, so persisting delivered W per node keeps those heat inputs exact, which justifies keeping power_use. Then I start questioning whether n_draw is truly necessary versus just recomputing W from req_eff and saturation, especially since PUMP's req is itself a throttle value that could change.

I decide to just keep `n_draw` since recomputing from throttle_pm gets messy, acknowledging this expands the cross-ADR footprint — ADR-0011 now needs two new node columns plus an e0 overlay for CABLE, which I'll flag as an assumption with a documented fallback. I then trace through the remaining cross-phase dependencies: `circ` computed in phase 5 feeds both heat capture and phase 9's consumption recompute cleanly since it's pure; atmosphere's fuel_puddle, scrubber O2 production, and breathed_mgu all rely on properly persisted counters; and the failure-to-power-hook transition correctly uses persisted state like forced_next, mode_key, isolated_at, hp, state, flags, and bands, with phase 0 to phase 2 staying within the same hook. I'm now considering whether there are any remaining cross-hook dependencies read by external consumers that I haven't accounted for.

Checking the suit's P/band reads at 6n+2 and the emitter's served reads, both confirm as pure and properly persisted, which lets me sketch out the full enumeration table for section 11 covering served, draw, load, T_mach/circ/Q_cap, island aliveness, heater duty, descriptor store, alarms, and more. This extends into the atmo tail at phase 7 handling COMP/BAND and stock buckets, and the failure tail at phase 11 handling hp changes from phase 8 and state/severity transitions from phase 9. I'm formalizing this as "bucket close-out" steps at the end of each hook, then updating the phase table's keys column so phase 0 marks NODE/EDGE directly for forced_mode/hp changes at write time, matching ADR-0011 §10's rule that marking happens inside the mutator or phase that changed the data.

Now I'm pinning down which phase "owns" each marking family: hp gets marked in phase 0 and phase 8 (not 11, since that's where it's just consumed), while the stock bucket gets marked across phases 0, 2, 3, 4, and 5 as each respective reconcile/battery/fuel/O2/reservoir write happens. I'm working out whether descriptor intensity changes need to be marked at phase 11 given the lag from earlier flow calculations, concluding it's fine since the failure-tracking poll only runs once per step.

I'm redrafting the "keys fired" table per phase: phase 0 handles NODE/EDGE for hp and forced_mode; phases 2-5 handle LOOP plus the corresponding stock bucket marks for power, fuel, O2, and coolant; phase 7 handles COMP/BAND; phase 8 handles hp again; and phase 9 handles state, forced mode, and SEAM markings.

I'm finishing the phase table (phase 10 is a no-op, phase 11 handles DESC only), which rules out the earlier assumption that phase 11 also touches hp. Then I move to cross-checking the registry row counts against the advisor's listed 28 rows across the lsg, interact, derelict, boarding, and webmap families, verifying my own tally of 28 matches plus the extra lsg-020 partial row bringing my total to 29, and I'm now double-checking how lsg-020's Planned ADR assignment fits into the covered/partial breakdown.

If a mutator reaches a hook with topo_dirty set and cause MUTATOR, that's a defect to flag in late_rebuilds. Phase-driven transitions get rebuilt at the head of the next Graph hook — so a phase 9 cable failure surfaces as a split island by phase 2 of the next cycle — while restores trigger an immediate full rebuild with the dirty flag cleared. ### 4. Topology refresh and derived caches (TR-lsg-010, TR-assembly-034)

**One function, two call sites.** `GraphDerived.ensure_derived(...)` is the single idempotent rebuild of every topology-dependent cache; it returns at once while `caches.topo_dirty` is clear. It is called (a) at the end of **every structural mutator** (M1 to M6, M8, M9, M19) and in `post_restore`, so a weld, cut, discard, install or valve flip is complete, with its caches, when the mutator returns (the weld-preview drag and `can_join` never pay a rebuild, and no hook can interleave with a mutator because the kernel is single-threaded); and (b) as the **head guard** of all three hooks (`GraphPropagate.enter`), which is the GDD's "at the head of whichever Graph hook first runs after a structural mutator". The guard exists for one legitimate case and one defect:

The three unconditional channels are **queued**, persisted (ADR-0011 § 3.8) and **drained only in phase 0**, so a Graph step is a function of the persisted state at its start (§ 11).

1. **`pending_load`:** for each entry in arrival order, resolve the node (a node salvaged or a section made dormant since is skipped and counted), set `req = clampi(load_req, 0, req_max)`, and mark `NODE` if the value changed. Entries name distinct nodes, so order does not matter to the result.
2. **`pending_draw`:** zero the whole `draw_grant` table, then sort the entries by the packed key `(cid << 24) | (crew << 8) | arrival_index` with a bounded insertion sort (a `for` loop with `break`, over `x.q_key`; probe (c): 4.0 microseconds at 16 entries, 32.8 at 56 in the editor, and the typical queue is a few entries) and walk them: `got = mini(mgu, n_o2[c])`, `n_o2[c] -= got`, `breathed_mgu[section] += got`, and `grant_req[crew] += mgu`, `grant_got[crew] += got`. ### 6. The mutator contract (TR-lsg-016)

The Graph registers **no command** (kernel H2); its mutators are plain methods of `GraphMutators` handed to the owning modules' `setup()` (ADR-0003 § 10). | M6 | `salvage_node` (`check_salvage_node`) | APPLY, HOOK | immediate | ADR-0011 § 5; EXOGENOUS flag on the node and its severed edges; rebuilds | `T`, `N/<id>` |
| M7 | `repair_step` (`check_repair_step`) | APPLY, HOOK | immediate | `hp`, `hp_cap`, `patched_at`; does not touch `state` (phase 9 re-evaluates) | `N`/`E` (`hp` bucket) |
| M8, M9 | `set_valve`, `set_breaker` | APPLY, HOOK | immediate | the OPEN or BREAKER_CLOSED flag; connectivity changes, so rebuilds; M9 close stamps `energised_at` on the branch's loads | `E`/`N`, `T` |
| M10 | `set_setpoint` | APPLY, HOOK | immediate | `req` of a PUMP (`throttle_pm`) or VENT (`setpoint_pp`), clamped; **not queued** | `N` |
| M11, M12 | `reset_node`, `cap_port` | APPLY, HOOK | immediate | clears SCRAM or FREEZE only if the clear condition holds (`BLOCKED` otherwise, a physical answer); CAPPED flag | `N` |
| M13 | `set_opening_area` | **APPLY only** | immediate | `area` (the only writer of `area`); no topology change | `E` |

- **No mutator is called from the Graph's own hooks**, and **no phase calls a mutator**: phases write their columns directly (they are writer files, ADR-0011 § 12.1) and mark keys themselves (§ 12). A mutator reads a phase's results only through persisted columns.
- **`M13` and Layout (ADR-0013).** M13 writes `area`; no phase ever does, so Layout's template-door state is untouched in P3, and `set_opening_area` is never called from a hook (ADR-0013's guideline). The door-motor power precondition is Interaction's, not the Graph's.
- **`M10` is immediate and `req` is persisted**, so a throttle change mid-step is seen by the next phase that reads `req`; the heat a machine injects is taken from the delivered power `n_draw` of the last solve (§ 11), not from `req`, so a mid-step change never creates or destroys energy.

### 7. The fairness gate (TR-lsg-013, TR-lsg-015)

The gate is a **floor applied at the moment damage is applied**, never a post-pass that rewrites `hp` afterwards: it limits the reduction and can never raise `hp` (D.9). The rule is one pure function so phase 8, M18 and the tests call identical code:

```gdscript
# src/shared/graph/graph_rules.gd
## Lowest hp an endogenous loss may leave behind; 0 means no floor (gate open).
static func gate_floor(hp_before: int, hull_or_seam: bool, gate_open: bool, hp_fail: int, breach_hp: int) -> int:
	if gate_open:
		return 0
	if hull_or_seam and hp_before >= breach_hp:
		return breach_hp                       # the LEAK -> BREACH escalation is gated
	if hp_before > hp_fail:
		return hp_fail + 1                     # FAILED/DESTROYED is gated
	return 1                                   # already FAILED: DESTROYED is gated

## hp left after applying a loss, never above hp_before.
static func apply_loss(hp_before: int, loss: int, floor_hp: int) -> int:
	return hp_before - mini(loss, maxi(0, hp_before - floor_hp))
```

- **`gate_open`** is `HAS_WARN ∧ step_no - warn_since >= W_MIN_STEPS` for a node, edge or seam, and the compartment tracker's bit and stamp for a compartment descriptor (LS-13 (b), D.11), with `W_MIN_STEPS` derived once at boot as `IntMath.floor_div(W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE, GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)` by the loader (not read from the registry by the Graph: `TICK_RATE` is on the OWN-lint token list of ADR-0011 § 12.2).
- **Evaluation order inside a step.** Phase 8 evaluates the gate from the `warn_since`/HAS_WARN that phase 9 of an **earlier** run (or M1) stamped; phase 9 then stamps this run's `sev`; phase 11 evaluates `gate_open` again for the descriptors. A warning that begins in phase 9 of step *s* therefore has `warn_elapsed` 0 at phase 11 of *s* and first opens the gate when `step_no - warn_since` reaches `W_MIN_STEPS` (D.11's worked examples are reproduced exactly: the overload cable is held on steps 70 to 100 and fails on step 101; the compartment alarm flips at step 125).
- **Held damage is gone.** The excess is discarded, never carried over; `GraphDiag.gate_holds` records `(subject, steps held)`; a subject already below its floor takes no further endogenous damage until the gate opens and is never moved.
- **EXOGENOUS bypass and the cause flag.** A damage source declares its cause. EXOGENOUS (floor 0): player verbs (cut, vent, salvage, the `INRUSH_STEPS` overload after a breaker close, tagged in phase 8 from `energised_at`), M17 RUPTURE and GOUGE, and M18 with `cause = EXOGENOUS`. The node/edge EXOGENOUS flag bit (ADR-0011 § 3.2, the descriptor's `cause`) is **set by an exogenous apply and cleared when the subject's dominant mode returns to 0 in phase 9 or its `hp` is repaired to `HP_OK`**, so it names the cause of the *current episode*: an endogenous wear tick on a ruptured pipe does not flip the descriptor back to ENDOGENOUS. (ADR-0011 Open Question 3 asked the GDD to name `cause` as persisted; this rule says when it clears. `gdd_sync`.) A cut completing on a running machine is therefore EXOGENOUS by M3/M6 setting the flag on what they sever: the Graph re-solves the island on its next power hook, dependants go STARVE (a status, not an `hp` change, so no gate and no minimum-warning wait), and the SEVERED descriptors carry `cause = EXOGENOUS`, which is what Attention reads to open no breach-window row (TR-boarding-039; Attention's own rule is ADR-0022).
- **Alarm eligibility.** `alarm_eligible = alarm_capable(mode) ∧ sev >= ALARM_SEV_MIN ∧ gate_open`, evaluated per descriptor in phase 11. `alarm_capable` is the closed LS-13 (a) set (modes 1 to 5, 7 to 9 and 20 to 23; never 6, 10, 24 to 27), held as `GraphIds.ALARM_CAPABLE_MASK` (a code-side rule, not tunable, bit `m` set for each capable mode `m`; boot checks it against the mode table's `alarm_capable` column, ADR-0007). **`alarm_sections()`** is a pure read: phase 11 rebuilds `caches.alarm_sections` (an ascending, duplicate-free `PackedInt32Array` of `section_id` built by one pass over the descriptor store, deduplicated by comparing with the last appended id, which is valid because the store is ordered by subject kind then subject id and the pass keeps a per-section seen byte), and `GraphView.alarm_sections(out)` copies it into the caller's buffer (ADR-0011 § 9.1). It is empty before the first gate opens and holds the section from the run the first capable descriptor's gate opens (the D.11 Example B behaviour).
- **Dormant sections** freeze `warn_since` (§ 10), so a dormant section's descriptors would never close their gate; `soonest_warning_remaining(loaded_only)` skips them when asked.

```gdscript
# src/shared/graph/graph_rules.gd
## Lowest hp an endogenous loss may leave behind; 0 means no floor (gate open).
static func gate_floor(hp_before: int, hull_or_seam: bool, gate_open: bool, hp_fail: int, breach_hp: int) -> int:
	if gate_open:
		return 0
	if hull_or_seam and hp_before >= breach_hp:
		return breach_hp                       # the LEAK -> BREACH escalation is gated
	if hp_before > hp_fail:
		return hp_fail + 1                     # FAILED/DESTROYED is gated
	return 1                                   # already FAILED: DESTROYED is gated

## hp left after applying a loss, never above hp_before.
static func apply_loss(hp_before: int, loss: int, floor_hp: int) -> int:
	return hp_before - mini(loss, maxi(0, hp_before - floor_hp))
```

### 4. Topology refresh and derived caches (TR-lsg-010, TR-assembly-034)

It is called (a) at the end of **every structural mutator** (M1 to M6, M8, M9, M19) and in `post_restore`, so a weld, cut, discard, install or valve flip is complete, with its caches, when the mutator returns (the weld-preview drag and `can_join` never pay a rebuild, and no hook can interleave with a mutator because the kernel is single-threaded); and (b) as the **head guard** of all three hooks (`GraphPropagate.enter`), which is the GDD's "at the head of whichever Graph hook first runs after a structural mutator". The guard exists for one legitimate case and one defect:

- **Phase-driven transitions (legitimate).** A phase-9 state change that alters connectivity (a CABLE, CABLE_JUNCTION, PIPE, DUCT or VALVE crossing the FAILED boundary, or a DESTROYED subject) sets `topo_dirty` with `topo_cause = PHASE`. The next hook's head guard rebuilds, so the power hook at the start of the next step solves a split island (C1, D.15 BROKEN-BREAKER: "on run 1 the island splits"). The hook sees the whole new topology, never half of it.
- **Defect.** A hook that finds `topo_dirty` with `topo_cause = MUTATOR` has met a structural mutator that forgot its own rebuild; the guard still rebuilds (so the run is correct) and increments `GraphDiag.late_rebuilds`, which every Graph test asserts is zero.

**What `ensure_derived` builds**, in this order, all into preallocated `GraphCaches` members sized by `size_derived()` (structural mutators and `post_restore` size them; the hook path never resizes): the four id-to-slot maps and the edge endpoint slots (ADR-0011 § 4.2); the **active lists** `active_nodes`, `active_edges`, `active_comps`, `active_seams` (ascending slot, tombstones and dormant sections excluded, § 10) and the typed sublists `store_slots` and `machine_slots`; `V` and `exposed_tiles` per compartment through `RoomSource`; the adjacency CSR; the loop **components** for loops 1 to 4 and, for POWER, the **trees** and `path_cap`; the POWER island list; and the sizes of the scratch and the descriptor store. `degrees` and `deg_max` are **not** cached: an OPENING counts toward a room's degree only while its `area` is above 0 and a hull segment only while it has a hole, and both change without a structural mutator (M13, a phase-9 breach), so phase 6 recomputes them in one O(E) pass at its head into scratch (a refinement of LS-8's phase 1; `gdd_sync`).

**Connectivity predicate (the one definition).** An edge joins its two endpoints in a loop's component only if: a VALVE is open; a CABLE or seam cable has `state` not FAILED/DESTROYED (its `cap` is positive); a PIPE, DUCT or FUEL PIPE has `state` not FAILED/DESTROYED; a CABLE_JUNCTION has its breaker closed; and a port is not CAPPED or OPEN_END for flow purposes. OPENINGs are the atmosphere's exchange links, not loop topology, and do not enter components. This single predicate is why TR-boarding-041 holds without a special case: an uncapped stub of a cut derelict leaks from the pool of **its own component**, which includes the home network's pool only while the seam VALVE is open, because a closed valve splits the component.

### 7. The fairness gate (TR-lsg-013, TR-lsg-015)

The gate is a **floor applied at the moment damage is applied**, never a post-pass that rewrites `hp` afterwards: it limits the reduction and can never raise `hp` (D.9). The rule is one pure function so phase 8, M18 and the tests call identical code:

```gdscript
# src/shared/graph/graph_rules.gd
## Lowest hp an endogenous loss may leave behind; 0 means no floor (gate open).
static func gate_floor(hp_before: int, hull_or_seam: bool, gate_open: bool, hp_fail: int, breach_hp: int) -> int:
	if gate_open:
		return 0
	if hull_or_seam and hp_before >= breach_hp:
		return breach_hp                       # the LEAK -> BREACH escalation is gated
	if hp_before > hp_fail:
		return hp_fail + 1                     # FAILED/DESTROYED is gated
	return 1                                   # already FAILED: DESTROYED is gated

## hp left after applying a loss; never above hp_before.
static func apply_loss(hp_before: int, loss: int, floor_hp: int) -> int:
	return hp_before - mini(loss, maxi(0, hp_before - floor_hp))
```

- **`gate_open`** is `HAS_WARN ∧ step_no - warn_since >= W_MIN_STEPS` for a node, edge or seam, and the compartment tracker's bit and stamp for a compartment descriptor (LS-13 (b), D.11). `W_MIN_STEPS` is derived once at boot as `IntMath.floor_div(W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE, GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)` by the loader and handed to the Graph in `GraphTuning`; the Graph never names `TICK_RATE` (ADR-0011 § 12.2 token list).
- **Evaluation order inside a step.** Phase 8 evaluates the gate from the `warn_since`/HAS_WARN that phase 9 of an **earlier** run (or M1) stamped; phase 9 then stamps this run's `sev`; phase 11 evaluates `gate_open` again for the descriptors. A warning that begins in phase 9 of step *s* therefore has `warn_elapsed` 0 at phase 11 of *s* and first opens the gate when `step_no - warn_since` reaches `W_MIN_STEPS`. D.11's worked examples are reproduced exactly: the overload cable is held on steps 70 to 100 and fails on step 101; the compartment alarm flips at step 125.
- **Held damage is gone.** The excess is discarded, never carried over; `GraphDiag.gate_holds` records the subject and the steps held; a subject already below its floor takes no further endogenous damage until the gate opens and is never moved.
- **EXOGENOUS bypass and the cause flag.** A damage source declares its cause. EXOGENOUS (floor 0): player verbs (cut, vent, salvage, the `INRUSH_STEPS` overload after a breaker close, tagged in phase 8 from `energised_at`), M17 RUPTURE and GOUGE, and M18 with `cause = EXOGENOUS`. The node and edge EXOGENOUS flag bit (ADR-0011 § 3.2, the descriptor's `cause`) is **set by an exogenous apply and cleared when the subject's dominant mode returns to 0 in phase 9 or its `hp` is repaired to `HP_OK`**, so it names the cause of the *current episode*: an endogenous wear tick on a ruptured pipe does not flip the descriptor back to ENDOGENOUS. (ADR-0011 Open Question 3 asked the GDD to name `cause` as persisted; this rule says when it clears. `gdd_sync`.) A cut completing on a running machine is EXOGENOUS because M3 and M6 set the flag on what they sever: the Graph re-solves the island on its next power hook, dependants go STARVE (a status, not an `hp` change, so no gate and no minimum-warning wait), and the SEVERED descriptors carry `cause = EXOGENOUS`, which is what Attention reads to open no breach-window row (TR-boarding-039; Attention's own rule is ADR-0022).
- **Alarm eligibility.** `alarm_eligible = alarm_capable(mode) ∧ sev >= ALARM_SEV_MIN ∧ gate_open`, evaluated per descriptor in phase 11. `alarm_capable` is the closed LS-13 (a) set (modes 1 to 5, 7 to 9 and 20 to 23; never 6, 10, 24 to 27), held as `GraphIds.ALARM_CAPABLE_MASK` (a code-side rule, not tunable, bit `m` set for each capable mode `m`; boot checks it against the mode table's `alarm_capable` column, ADR-0007). **`alarm_sections()`** is a pure read: phase 11 sets a per-section seen byte in scratch during its single pass over the descriptor store and then writes `caches.alarm_sections` by walking the sections table in ascending id, so the list is ascending and duplicate-free by construction; `GraphView.alarm_sections(out)` copies it into the caller's buffer (ADR-0011 § 9.1). It is empty before the first capable descriptor's gate opens and holds the section from that run (the D.11 Example B behaviour).
- **Dormant sections** freeze `warn_since` (§ 10), so a dormant section's descriptors would never close their gate; `soonest_warning_remaining(loaded_only)` skips them when asked.
